status: One regular proposal; two literal Story holds and three concise source/canon holds. Zero author admissions.

candidates.subject: red-eyed tree frog
candidates.title: Before feet
candidates.body:
A small trembling came through the clear wall. Then another. I stopped turning.

The trembling grew until there was nowhere in the egg it did not reach. I pressed my face outward and waited while the whole soft place shook around me.

It went on for so long that I curled my tail back beside my face.

Eventually the shaking thinned and stopped.

Someone next to me wriggled. A little movement reached me through the jelly. I turned too.

For a while we disturbed only each other.
candidates.visibleScene: A hanging clutch of translucent eggs beneath a green leaf contains well-developed brown embryos with visible eyes and curled tails. Individual capsules sit close together in a gelatinous mass. Backlighting reveals bodies and membranes; no adult, predator or hatching is pictured.
candidates.fictionBoundary: An imagined pre-hatching vignette, not a claim adult frogs remember embryonic events. The storm, exact timing, sensing a particular neighbor and subjective relief are fictional. Embryonic vibration sensing and transmission of routine embryo movements through clutches are supported by primary research. The photograph earns life within the connected clutch; it does not prove any recorded storm. No egg is said to hatch and exact hatching competence or age in days is not assigned.
candidates.canon: Existing female Ada Dew, Tortuguero lowland forest Costa Rica (10.542,-83.502). Insert earliest, before every adult episode. Preserve her avatar and all literal prior passages. Eggs cannot be sexed visually; narrating one as the future female is fiction consistent with the species and life stage. Sarapiqui is source provenance, not a relocation. No parent identity, sibling count, remembered adult event or hatching fate is added.
candidates.payoff: A body not yet outside its egg waits through a large disturbance. When quiet returns, the tiny movement of another enclosed body becomes company. Her later sensitivity to interruptions has an intimate earlier counterpart without turning the event into an explanation of her personality.
candidates.reviewFlag: The actual clutch and embryos are strong, with some soft peripheral capsules. Unlike held Moss117, no absent departing hatchling carries the climax. Nonetheless the disturbance is wholly fictional; lead should judge whether the pictured shared membranes and curled bodies sufficiently carry this sensory vignette.

holds.title: Two bodies at the turn
holds.body:
I went to turn around and found his arms under mine.

Tried the other way. He came too.

We've been facing the same patch of darkness for some time. I had wanted him to stay. I'm trying to move without making it look as though I've changed my mind.
holds.reason: Actual literal draft evaluated. Amplexus is clearly pictured, but this version leans on a familiar human romantic misunderstanding and social self-consciousness. It does not yet make enough of the female carrying the male. Do not count a routine direction change as a second event merely because the source is sound.

holds.title: The other warm rock
holds.body:
Waited for the sun to reach the next rock. Jumped as soon as it did.

Landed on stone that was still cold.

I had been watching the light so carefully that I'd left a warm place to meet it.
holds.reason: Actual draft evaluated. Clear airborne hyrax supports a leap, with deliberate panning blur and a small retained photographer mark. The destination-temperature mistake is a mild weather errand and ends by explaining itself. It does not justify admission beside his stronger existing physical episodes.

Animal heavily obscured by foreground branches. Search water led to a place-name match, not swimming. No swimming fiction attached. Observation46811553 also explicitly mainland subspecies T. a. aculeatus; no attempt to swap it for Tasmanian Orla.
Pairs and resting groups offer company, but would repeat his existing leaning youngster or paired watch mechanisms. No new narrative forced from these.
An initial discovery query mistakenly used a burrowing owl taxon. Read current Otis arc and corrected: Otis is an American white pelican. No owl photograph was downloaded, used or attributed to Otis.

biologySources.title: Is it safe? Red-eyed treefrog embryos assessing predation risk use two features of rain vibrations to avoid false alarms
biologySources.authors: Michael S. Caldwell, J. Gregory McDaniel, Karen M. Warkentin
biologySources.review: Primary full-text PDF opened successfully through web tool. Page256 explicitly includes routine embryo movements among causes of clutch vibrations and describes vibration-based discrimination. Rain intensity buildup and higher frequencies can inhibit escape hatching. Direct local PDF download later returned403; stopped without retry. No local PDF is claimed.
biologySources.boundary: Fiction does not quote the study, claim conscious human reasoning, prescribe exact embryo age, or identify a real weather event. Study terminology is confined to evidence.
